definition: Advanced Host Controller Interface. The legacy protocol for SATA devices, replaced by NVMe for high-performance SSDs.
Annualized Failure Rate. The expected percentage of units that fail in one year, derived from MTBF: `AFR = (8,760 ÷ MTBF) × 100%`. A 1.5M hour MTBF equals approximately 0.58% AFR.
Addressable RGB. Per-LED lighting control allowing complex effects and patterns independent of neighbor LEDs.
A disk benchmarking tool that measures performance across various transfer sizes.
The rate at which data can be transferred, typically measured in MB/s or GB/s.
A collection of memory banks in DDR4/DDR5 that can operate with partial independence. DDR5 doubles bank groups from 4 to 8 vs. DDR4.
Basic Input/Output System. Firmware that initializes hardware during boot. Modern systems use UEFI.
The storage device containing the operating system.
Temporary storage area used to compensate for speed differences between components.
A sequence of data transfers triggered by a single command in DRAM.
Fast memory that stores frequently accessed data for quicker retrieval.

Compression Attached Memory Module 2. An emerging memory form factor that mounts flat to the motherboard using compression contacts rather than traditional slots. Thinner than SO-DIMM, enables DDR5-6400+ in laptops, and provides dual-channel operation from a single module. Not compatible with SO-DIMM or UDIMM. Gaining adoption in premium laptops; desktop CAM
The delay between a read command and data output in memory. Measured in clock cycles — use true latency (ns) for real comparisons. See CAS Latency Explained.
An independent data path between the CPU and memory. Dual-channel = two paths for doubled bandwidth.
Clock signal. The timing reference for synchronous memory operations.
The processor on an SSD that manages NAND operations, error correction, wear leveling, and host communication.
TwinMOS flagship Gen5 NVMe SSD with up to 14,000 MB/s sequential read speeds. See CoreX Pro Gen5.

Clock Driver DIMM. An advanced DDR5 module variant with an integrated clock buffer (CKD) chip that improves signal integrity at extreme frequencies (DDR5-7200+). Required for Intel Core Ultra 200S Plus platforms targeting DDR5-7200 natively. Functionally compatible with standard DDR5 systems but does not offer CUDIMM advantages there.
Double Data Rate. Memory that transfers data on both rising and falling clock edges, doubling effective bandwidth vs. SDR.
Fourth generation DDR memory (1.2V, up to DDR4-3200 standard; DDR4-5333+ overclocked).
Fifth generation DDR memory (1.1V, DDR5-4800+ standard, dual 32-bit subchannels, on-die ECC, PMIC). See What is DDR5?.

Sixth generation DDR memory. Desktop specification finalizing late 2025/early 2026; consumer platform adoption expected 2027+. Speed targets: 12,800+ MT/s base. LPDDR6 was standardized by JEDEC in July 2025.

Microsoft API (current version 1.4) allowing GPUs to load compressed game assets directly from NVMe SSDs, bypassing CPU decompression. Requires NVMe (SATA incompatible). Includes Zstd compression support. See Best SSD for Gaming.
Dual In-line Memory Module. Standard desktop memory stick (also called UDIMM).
Dynamic Random-Access Memory. Volatile memory used as system RAM.
Drive Writes Per Day. Enterprise SSD endurance metric indicating how many times the full capacity can be written daily over the warranty period.
Error-Correcting Code. Memory that detects and corrects data errors. See What is ECC Memory?.
Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory.
The total amount of data that can be written to an SSD before reaching its wear limit (TBW).
AMD EXtended Profiles for Overclocking. AMD's open-standard DDR5 memory profile system, optimized for Ryzen platforms with Infinity Fabric settings. See What is AMD EXPO?.
The process of clearing a NAND block (minimum erase unit) to prepare it for new writes.
Software embedded in hardware devices controlling their operation.
Failures In Time. Failures per billion device-hours. `MTBF = 1,000,000,000 ÷ FIT`.
Non-volatile memory technology used in SSDs (NAND flash).
Physical dimensions and connector type of a component (e.g., M.2 2280, M.2 2230, SO-DIMM).
Front Side Bus. Legacy term for CPU-to-chipset connection.
Flash Translation Layer. SSD firmware that maps logical addresses to physical NAND locations, enabling wear leveling and garbage collection.
SSD background process that reclaims space by consolidating valid pages and erasing blocks containing stale data. See TRIM and Garbage Collection.
Gigabytes per second. Unit of data transfer rate.
PCIe generations, each doubling bandwidth per lane. Gen5 is the current consumer peak at ~16 GB/s (x4 configuration).
Ultra-thin thermal solution using graphene's exceptional thermal conductivity (~5,300 W/mK vs. aluminum's ~237 W/mK). See What is a Graphene Heatsink?.
Hard Disk Drive. Mechanical storage with spinning magnetic platters.
A component that dissipates heat from hot devices through conduction and convection.

Host Memory Buffer. NVMe 1.2+ feature allowing DRAM-less SSDs to borrow 16–128 MB of system RAM for FTL caching. Improves random performance vs. no cache (200K–400K IOPS vs. 30K–80K IOPS). See What is HMB?.
TwinMOS SATA SSD delivering up to 580/550 MB/s read/write speeds. See Hyper H2 Ultra.
Input/Output. Data transfer between a device and the rest of the system.
Integrated Circuit. A chip containing miniaturized electronic circuits.
Input/Output Operations Per Second. The key measure of random storage performance.
Joint Electron Device Engineering Council. The standards body that defines DRAM and memory specifications globally.
Unit of energy; relevant for understanding power consumption and heat output.
Kilobyte. 1,024 bytes.
Physical notches on connectors preventing incorrect insertion (e.g., M.2 B-key vs. M-key, DDR4 vs. DDR5 notch positions).
Delay between a request and its response. Lower is better for responsiveness.
Logical Block Addressing. How the OS addresses storage locations, which the SSD maps to physical NAND via FTL.
Low-Density Parity Check. Advanced error correction algorithm used in modern SSD controllers.
TwinMOS DRAM warranty covering the useful life of the product.
Low Power DDR6. Mobile memory standard standardized by JEDEC in July 2025. Starting speeds: 10,667 MT/s, scaling toward 17,000+ MT/s. Informs desktop DDR6 architecture.
Compact form factor for SSDs and wireless cards, connecting via PCIe (NVMe) or SATA. Common lengths: 2280 (80 mm) and 2230 (30 mm).
The SSD's Flash Translation Layer data structure translating logical addresses to physical NAND locations.
Megabytes per second. Unit of data transfer rate.
CPU-integrated logic managing all DRAM operations, timing, and error correction.
Multi-Level Cell. NAND storing 2 bits per cell. Better endurance than TLC/QLC; mostly replaced in consumer products.
Mean Time Between Failures. Statistical measure of hardware reliability expressed in hours. For non-repairable items (SSDs), technically MTTF, but the industry uses MTBF for both. See What is MTBF?.

Mean Time To Failure. The technically correct reliability metric for non-repairable items like SSDs (vs. MTBF for repairable systems). In practice, the storage industry uses "MTBF" for both. `AFR = (8,760 ÷ MTTF) × 100%`.
Megatransfers per second. The accurate way to express DDR memory data rates (e.g., DDR5-6000 = 6,000 MT/s).
Type of flash memory used in SSDs. Named after the NAND logic gate. Varieties: SLC, MLC, TLC, QLC.
Native Command Queuing. SATA feature for reordering commands to optimize mechanical drive performance; less relevant for SSDs.
Nanometer. Unit of measurement for semiconductor process nodes (e.g., 176-layer NAND, 12nm controller).
Non-Volatile Memory Express. High-performance protocol for PCIe SSDs. Supports 64K queues × 64K commands per queue. See What is NVMe?.
Error correction built into every DDR5 memory chip as a standard feature. Corrects single-bit errors transparently with no performance penalty. See On-Die ECC Explained.
Extra NAND capacity beyond the advertised drive size, reserved for wear leveling, garbage collection, and spare block management.
The smallest writable unit in NAND flash (typically 4–16 KB).
Peripheral Component Interconnect Express. High-speed serial expansion bus. Each generation doubles per-lane bandwidth. See What is PCIe?.
Power Management Integrated Circuit. On-module voltage regulator standard on DDR5, enabling granular power control and improved stability. See PMIC Explained.
Memory architecture that fetches multiple bits per internal clock cycle to match bus width.
Quad-Level Cell. NAND storing 4 bits per cell. Highest density, lowest endurance; common in high-capacity consumer drives.
Number of pending I/O operations a storage device handles simultaneously.
Redundant Array of Independent Disks. Multiple drives combined for performance or redundancy.
Random Access Memory. Volatile working memory; data lost on power loss.
Access pattern reading/writing scattered non-sequential locations. Measured in IOPS; harder for storage than sequential.
A 64-bit wide logical memory device on a DIMM.
DRAM maintenance operation rewriting cells to prevent charge decay; occurs thousands of times per second automatically.
Red Green Blue. Lighting system in PC components for visual customization.
NVIDIA's Blackwell-architecture GPU lineup (2025): RTX 5060 ($299), RTX 5060 Ti ($429), RTX 5070 ($549), RTX 5080 ($999), RTX 5090 ($1,999+). Features DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation AI upscaling.
AMD's RDNA 4 GPU lineup (2025), including RX 9070 (~$449) and RX 9070 XT (~$499). Supports FSR 4 AI upscaling.
Serial ATA. Storage interface originally designed for hard drives; maximum throughput ~580 MB/s. Incompatible with DirectStorage. See What is a SATA SSD?.
Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection. Common ECC algorithm.
Access pattern reading/writing contiguous data blocks. Faster than random for any storage type.
Single-Level Cell. NAND storing 1 bit per cell. Fastest and most durable NAND type; used as SLC cache in consumer TLC drives.
Self-Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting Technology. Drive health monitoring standard. See What is SMART Monitoring?.
Small Outline DIMM. Laptop/mini-PC memory module, approximately half the length of UDIMM.
Solid State Drive. Storage using NAND flash with no moving parts; dramatically faster and more durable than HDDs.
Terabytes Written. SSD endurance rating indicating total data writable before reaching wear limit.
Automatic performance reduction to prevent component damage from overheating.
Triple-Level Cell. NAND storing 3 bits per cell. Current consumer standard; good balance of density, cost, and endurance.
ATA command (NVMe: Deallocate) informing the SSD which logical blocks the OS considers free. Reduces write amplification and extends endurance. See TRIM and Garbage Collection.
Actual response time in nanoseconds: `(CAS Latency × 2000) ÷ Speed (MT/s)`. More meaningful than the raw CL number for cross-generation comparisons.
Founded 1998. Global memory and storage manufacturer headquartered in Dubai, serving 93+ countries.
Unbuffered DIMM. Standard full-size desktop memory module (~133 mm long, 288 pins for DDR5).
Uninterruptible Power Supply. Battery backup protecting systems from power outages and transients.
Universal Serial Bus. Common peripheral connection standard.
TwinMOS DDR5 memory series (DDR5-5600 CL28 and DDR5-6000 CL30), available in RGB and standard heatsink variants. See VOLTX DDR5.
Electrical potential difference driving current flow. Lower voltage = less heat and power consumption.

Write Amplification Factor. Ratio of physical NAND writes to logical host writes. A WAF of 1.0 is ideal; random workloads typically produce WAF of 2–5; drives without TRIM can reach WAF of 10+. Lower WAF extends NAND endurance.
Technique distributing writes evenly across all NAND blocks to prevent premature wear of frequently written locations. See What is Wear Leveling?.
See WAF. The extra writes the SSD controller performs (for garbage collection, wear leveling, etc.) beyond what the host requested.
Extreme Memory Profile. Intel's standard for storing tested overclocking profiles on memory modules. XMP 3.0 for DDR5 supports up to 5 profiles with CRC integrity. See What is XMP?.
TwinMOS PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD with up to 7,500/6,800 MB/s sequential read/write speeds and graphene heatsink. See Xtreme Gen4.
Percentage of manufactured chips that pass quality testing and reach market.
Thickness measurement, often used for low-profile SSDs and memory modules.
Overwriting all drive data with zeros. A method of secure erasure.
Zoned Namespace. NVMe 2.0 feature organizing SSDs into append-only zones for reduced write amplification in workload-optimized environments.

Zstandard. A modern lossless compression algorithm developed by Facebook (Meta). Used in Microsoft DirectStorage 1.4 for GPU-decompressed asset streaming. Offers higher compression ratios and faster decompression than previous game asset formats.
